answer.rationale: P99 latency climbing 5x above target correlates directly with release 2 hours ago during heavy settlement writes. Memory_b1 shows rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; memory_b6 demonstrates staged release gating catches regressions. Current timing (release → latency degradation) and load conditions (peak settlement traffic) suggest the release introduced write path regression. Rollback is the highest-probability intervention to restore latency on the critical write path while settlement peak is still active. Verification of memory_b1 confirms rollback execution can complete without customer impact under load. Scale as standard_experiment acknowledges we have one intervention window; rollback completes fast and preserves ability to re-release if rollback itself fails. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) or read replica routing (memory_b5) address symptoms but not root cause when release timing is this tight. Regional failover (memory_b2) risks writes if not perfectly coordinated during peak. Capacity addition (memory_b3) helps future peaks but not immediate latency.
